facts.fact: William F. Mitchell, 1972, a Suffolk County Parks course where the Peconic River opens into Flanders Bay.
Long Island duck farming grew after the American Pekin arrived in 1873; about 90 Suffolk farms raised three million ducks a year in 1939. The Big Duck was built in Riverhead in 1931.

current.subject: A knapped flint arrowhead pointing right.
current.weaknesses: Sideways and grey; reads as a fish or a jet.

concepts.name: The Knapped Point
concepts.rationale: An upright, corner-notched projectile point with its flake scars shown facet by facet.
concepts.symbolism: Deep human history on the Peconic.
concepts.tradeoffs: Native imagery needs care; the artefact is drawn generically, not as a tribal symbol.

concepts.name: The Long Island Duckling
concepts.rationale: A white Pekin duck on the bay shore: Riverhead's duck-farming century.
concepts.tradeoffs: Keep clear of the Long Island Ducks baseball mascot.

recommendation: Concept 2. The duck is the area's own story and avoids leaning on Native imagery.
